content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs, and built a full source ledger against the disclosure and the (truncated) USER conversation passage.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. All 22 claims (independent claims 1, 13, 18 and every dependent limitation), all 27 entries of draft/numerals.md, every numbered part as it appears in each of the seven figure briefs, the Brief Description of the Drawings, the Summary, the Detailed Description, and the Abstract were checked one by one against affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md (the conversation file is a verbatim, truncated subset of it; input/brief.md was used only for formalities). Substantive matter traces cleanly: rail/upper face/lower face/longitudinal slot and printed distance marks beside the slot; fixed-yet-reversible fence at the first end with two screws in two corresponding holes and a downwardly projecting portion that moves from one longitudinal side to the other; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing separation; two separate guide carriages with lower keys in the slot that block rotation while permitting sliding; one cylindrical drill bushing per carriage with a vertical bore passing completely through and registering with the slot, the two bores parallel and perpendicular to the flat lower face; threaded clamp knob above the rail with a shank through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below; per-carriage pointers aligned with their bore axes and read against the same marks, their difference being center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index; the recited method sequence; rigid polymer or metal for the listed parts with hardened-metal replaceable bushings; and the no-motor/battery/sensor/network negative limitation. No dimensions, angles, proportions, tapers, depths, or contact topologies beyond the source appear anywhere; the schematic block/round-body/rectangular-body outlines in FIGS. 1, 2 and 4 are labeled "shown schematically", add no function, and are not verbalized in the claims or description, and the application text contains no "by way of example" or "any outline" language added to justify a render. Numeral hygiene checked: each numeral denotes exactly one part across the table, the description, and every figure list; every numeral appears in at least one figure and in the description; every parenthetical figure cross-reference (12→FIG. 3, 14→FIG. 4, 16/18→FIG. 2, 24/26/94→FIG. 7, 34/36→FIG. 6, 40→FIG. 4, 52/54/58/60→FIG. 5, 72/74/78/80→FIG. 3) resolves to a figure that lists that numeral. Section-line designations 3-3 and 5-5 are used identically in the source view (FIG. 2), the resulting views (FIGS. 3 and 5), and the Brief Description; the stepped offset legs are a necessary consequence of both the bore and the knob shank passing through the same narrow slot. Viewing directions are mutually consistent (FIGS. 3, 4 and 5 all look from the second end toward the first, which puts the workpiece edge on the left in FIG. 4 as briefed). No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, or unresolved alternative remains. Two verified internal-text problems are reported, both minor: FIG. 7 assigns the pencil centerline 94 an orientation and placement that cannot satisfy the description's and claim 6's requirement that the transverse center index 24 (at the midpoint) and the sight notch 26 (at the second end) be aligned together with that one straight line; and the Detailed Description introduces the unnumbered, undefined term "the reference face" for the numbered downwardly projecting portion 32. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced to the inventor, per instruction.

findings.title: FIG. 7 places centerline 94 so that the sight notch 26 cannot be aligned with it, contradicting the description and claim 6
findings.where: figures/FIG-7.md (centerline 94 paragraph, read against draft/08-detailed-description.md, FIG. 7 paragraph, and draft/09-claims.md claim 6)
findings.detail: The figure brief fixes centerline 94 as "running transverse to the length of the rail 10 in line with the transverse center index 24", and separately places index 24 "in the left part of the fragment, well away from the second end of the rail 10" while sight notch 26 is "formed in the second end of the rail 10". A single straight transverse line registered on the index at the midpoint therefore cannot also register on a notch located a substantial distance away at the second end. The description states "The transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 are aligned with one another, and the user aligns the transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 with the centerline 94 before drilling", and claim 6 recites "the sight notch and the transverse center index are alignable together with a centerline marked on the front face of the workpiece". FIG. 7 is the very view designated to show that alignment (draft/07-drawings.md: "showing the transverse center index and the sight notch"), so as briefed it will depict the notch off the centerline. The disclosure supplies both halves of the relationship ("A shallow V-shaped sight notch is formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the center index"; "The user can align the center index and the sight notch with a pencil centerline on the workpiece") but never states the orientation of the centerline; the transverse orientation is the figure brief's own addition and is what makes the depiction self-contradictory.
findings.evidence: FIG-7.md: "A centerline 94 is a straight pencil line drawn on the workpiece 90 alone, running transverse to the length of the rail 10 in line with the transverse center index 24, visible on the workpiece 90 on both long sides of the rail 10 and hidden where the rail 10 covers it." vs. FIG-7.md: "A transverse center index 24 ... in the left part of the fragment, well away from the second end of the rail 10" and "A sight notch 26 is a shallow V-shaped notch formed in the second end of the rail 10". Description: "The transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 are aligned with one another, and the user aligns the transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 with the centerline 94 before drilling." Nearest source, which does not state any centerline orientation: "The user can align the center index and the sight notch with a pencil centerline on the workpiece before tightening both carriage knobs."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-7.md, delete the unsourced orientation and placement clause and replace the sentence with: "A centerline 94 is a straight pencil line drawn on the workpiece 90 alone, aligned with the transverse center index 24 and with the sight notch 26, and visible on the workpiece 90 where the rail 10 does not cover it." Make no change to the description or to claim 6, which recite the source relationship.

findings.title: Undefined term "the reference face" used for the numbered downwardly projecting portion 32
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, last sentence of the paragraph beginning "The reversible mounting of the fence 30 addresses a practical difficulty"
findings.detail: The element that moves from one longitudinal side of the rail to the other on reversal is identified everywhere else in the application as "the downwardly projecting portion 32" (Summary, Detailed Description, claims 1, 7, 13, 15, 16, 18, 19, 20, and figure briefs 1, 4 and 6). This one sentence renames it "the reference face", a term that appears nowhere else, has no antecedent, and carries no reference numeral, so the same structure is designated by two different names within the same section.
findings.evidence: Draft: "Reversing the fence 30 alone moves the reference face to the other longitudinal side of the rail 10 while leaving the rail 10, the distance marks 18, and the carriage settings undisturbed." Compare the immediately preceding paragraph: "in that second orientation the downwardly projecting portion 32 lies on the opposite second longitudinal side of the rail 10", and claim 1: "a second orientation in which the downwardly projecting portion lies on the second longitudinal side of the rail".
findings.fix: Replace "the reference face" with "the downwardly projecting portion 32" so the sentence reads: "Reversing the fence 30 alone moves the downwardly projecting portion 32 to the other longitudinal side of the rail 10 while leaving the rail 10, the distance marks 18, and the carriage settings undisturbed."
